panels.title: Can people sign in? The sign-in robots every five minutes, the codes going out, the outside checks, the sign-in alerts
Member robot
panels.description: The members' sign-in robot (`synthetics-member-sign-in`, SR-OR-1): every five minutes it signs in on the public portal as a browser does, with a software passkey, reads `/auth/me` and signs out; each run writes one result line (`synthetic_results`). now, worst first: ✕ Failing, red, while `signin-failing` is true (2 failed checks and no pass in 11 minutes, one of them not a lockout: it pages, urgent); ✕ Locked out, red (2 lockouts or rate limits and no pass in 11 minutes: `signin-robot-locked-out`, urgent); ✕ Not reporting, red (no result line for 16 minutes: `signin-silent`, urgent); ⚠ Robot broken, amber (the runner's own fault in 11 minutes: `signin-robot-broken`, can wait); ⚠ Failed once, amber (a failed check in 11 minutes, not a page: a look); ⚠ Off over a day, amber (auth's switch has refused it for 24 hours with no pass: `signin-checks-off`, a notice); Switched off (auth's switch refused it in 11 minutes and nothing passed: `disabled`, no verdict); ✓ Signing in, teal (a pass in 16 minutes). Right after it is unpaused it reads ✕ Not reporting until its first run's line lands (five to seven minutes), where its page waits ten. last pass: within 6 or 16 minutes, within the hour, earlier today, or none in 24 h. 24 h: passes over passes and failures (a skip or the runner's own error is no verdict). "not deployed" while tpa-platform has not built it (signin_robots_enabled; the service's TPA_SIGNIN_ROBOTS), "paused" while its schedule is paused, "database stopped" while auth-db is: in no colour, and nothing is asked of Cloud Monitoring while it is not deployed. The link opens its runs on the Sign-in page.

panels.title: Texted codes (24 h)
panels.description: Members' and brokers' texted sign-in codes in the last 24 hours. delivered and not delivered: as Twilio reported each one back to auth's messenger (`auth_texts_reported`, by its closed word; `auth-texts-not-delivered` at five in an hour, `auth-texts-blocked`, urgent, when the carriers refuse the line). not sent: never handed to Twilio, for the number's or the account's reason (`auth_texts_not_sent`) or because the vendor or the path refused or did not answer (`auth_message_vendor_failures` on the sms lane; `sign-in-message-vendor`, urgent, at five in 15 minutes). A text whose delivery is never read back counts in none of these. Each member's own status is in their Notifications in ops.

panels.title: Emails (24 h)
panels.description: Sign-in emails (invitations, resets, codes) in the last 24 hours that did not go: refused or never answered by SendGrid or the path (`auth_message_vendor_failures` on the email lane; `sign-in-message-vendor`, urgent, at five in 15 minutes), and addressed to an address that cannot be delivered to (`auth_email_undeliverable`). No counter counts the emails sent: auth writes no line per email, so none going wrong reads as none here. A message of either kind waiting too long is the Sign-in alerts tile's (`auth-messages-stalled`).

panels.title: Outside checks
panels.description: The two outside checks on the portal host (D-335), each from three US regions every minute, as their outage policies read them (each region's latest result over 20 minutes, the regions failing counted): sign-in (`/auth/me`): auth's own 401 to a GET of /auth/me with no session: the address, the certificate, Cloud Armor, web's proxy to auth, auth and auth-db; portal (`/tpa/`): a 200 whose page holds the portal's <base href="/tpa/": the members' and brokers' portal itself, from web. ✕ failing, red, when more than 1 region fails (`outage: <host><path>` pages, urgent); ⚠ 1 region, amber (does not page); ✓ passing, teal; missing when a check reported nothing in that window (not built, or not reporting).

panels.title: Email checks
panels.description: The hourly mail check (tpa-platform D-400): records sends one check email an hour on each lane through the queues real emails take, invites through the opening-email chain and auth's messenger, notices through records' outbox and connectors, both to SendGrid; a Google-managed inbox counts each one whose DKIM signature proves we sent it (`mail_check_arrived`). invites and notices: ✓ arriving while a check of that lane arrived in the last 2 h 15 min, ✕ none in 2 h 15 min, red, as the urgent `mail-check-invites-missing` and `mail-check-notices-missing` read it (two hourly checks in a row; one late check is not a failure). refused (24 h): deliveries the inbox refused (`mail_check_refused`, by reason: not one of its addresses, not the check's subject, a signature missing, not ours or not verifying, a check older than a day or ahead of the clock, any request but Google's mail delivery). When each lane last arrived is Last check, beside this tile.

panels.title: Last check
panels.description: When each lane's newest mail check arrived in the inbox (`mail_check_arrived`, tpa-platform D-400), as a time ago: about an hour at most while it runs. A lane with none in 24 hours is missing here; Email checks beside it then reads ✕ and its urgent policy has opened.

panels.title: Email delivery (24 h)
panels.description: What SendGrid reported back in the last 24 hours, as records stored each signed report (`records_vendor_events`, by SendGrid's event and the kind of email records matched it to). delivered: to the recipient's server, every email (opening emails, notices, sign-in messages, the hourly mail checks and any records could not match). bounced or dropped, and spam reports: real emails alone, as `email-delivery-failed` counts them (its window is an hour): bounced, the address takes no mail; dropped, SendGrid would not send, most often an address it suppressed after an earlier bounce; a spam report, the person marked it so. Who and which email is the ops portal's delivery state and SendGrid's own activity feed, never this tile. None of these counts until SendGrid's signed reports reach records.

panels.title: Sign-in alerts
panels.description: The sign-in alerts that hold now, each its policy's own rule read from the same counters and windows, so a red row here is what pages (urgent: PagerDuty high urgency; can wait; a notice: email and Slack). This site cannot list incidents (Grafana's Cloud Monitoring datasource reads metrics only): the incidents, who has them and when they closed are PagerDuty's (the page's PagerDuty link). The robots' rules (urgent unless said): two failed checks and no pass in 11 minutes, one not a lockout (`signin-failing`); two lockouts or rate limits and no pass (`signin-robot-locked-out`); no result for 16 minutes while it runs (`signin-silent`); the runner's own fault (`signin-robot-broken`, can wait); switched off a day (`signin-checks-off`, a notice); anyone but the robots reading a robot's secret (`signin-robot-secret-read`); a robot's right password or live sign-in challenge used anywhere but its runner, any one in 5 minutes (`signin-robot-foreign-password`: somebody holds a robot's login; auth refused it); a wrong password at a robot's own address from elsewhere, any one in 15 minutes (`signin-robot-foreign-guess`, can wait: somebody learned the address). Those three are read while the robots' secrets exist, paused or not. A robot not deployed, paused or with auth-db stopped asks nothing of its own and is never silent. The messenger: five or more sends refused or unanswered by a vendor on one lane in 15 minutes (`sign-in-message-vendor`); the oldest message waiting above 120 s (`auth-messages-stalled`; read over its last 2 minutes, where the policy wants each minute above, so a row here can lead its page by a minute); the carriers refusing the texts' line, one `toll_free_unverified` or 3 `carrier_filtered` and more than half of the texts in an hour (`auth-texts-blocked`); `auth-outbox-publisher` with no instance for 5 minutes (its `has no instance`). The outside checks: more than one region failing on the portal host's `/auth/me` or `/tpa/` (`outage`). "? Can't tell": nothing arrived, or the queries failed.

panels.title: auth-db backups (30 h)
panels.description: auth-db's successful automated backups in the last 30 hours (`sql_automated_backups`, windowStatus STATUS_SUCCEEDED) and its failed ones (`sql_backup_failures`). The alert, `auth-db-backup-missing` (urgent), judges today's backup, from 14:00 UTC: the window from 09:00 UTC closed an hour before with no successful backup while the instance was up all day. This tile shows a successful backup in the last 30 hours, so a missed night turns it red about two hours after the page (30 hours after the night before's backup). One backup a night, starting in a four-hour window from 09:00 UTC: two have landed up to 26.1 hours apart, so a healthy instance always has one in 30 hours. ✕ none in 30 h, red: none while auth-db reported for 29 of the 30 hours or more; an instance started since reads "no backup yet". ✕ a backup failed, red: its newest failure (`auth-db-backup-failed`) is later than its newest success, each by the hour, so a failed attempt that a later attempt made good reads ✓ backed up, and a night that failed reads ✕ at once. The failed count, red from one, counts every failed entry in the 30 hours: one bad night writes several failed attempts and a final failure, so it is entries, not nights. ✓ backed up. Point-in-time recovery replays its seven days of logs from a backup taken before the minute chosen. "database stopped": stopped on purpose (its activation policy NEVER; the service's TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES). "not reporting": no value, and not listed as stopped: not built (cc-db exists with the staffed desk only), or reporting nothing. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).
